title: Le Palais de Continuité
text: Le Palais de Continuité The Palace of Continuity Location Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne, Jardin Type Seat of Government, Executive Complex, National Symbol Population Approximately 35,000 permanent staff Security Level Extreme Primary Authority Office of the Supreme Presidency Current Supreme President Leo Duprey Contents [Overview]( overview) [Session 1 Note]( session 1 note) [History]( history) [Colonial Administration (Years 0 120)]( colonial administration years 0 120) [The Unification Crisis (Year 147)]( the unification crisis year 147) [The Century of Planning (Years 280 450)]( the century of planning years 280 450) [Modern Era]( modern era) [Architecture]( architecture) [Major Facilities]( major facilities) [Office of the Supreme Presidency]( office of the supreme presidency) [Chamber of Continuity]( chamber of continuity) [Hall of Founders]( hall of founders) [Directorate Wing]( directorate wing) [Archives of Continuity]( archives of continuity) [Government Functions]( government functions) [Executive Administration]( executive administration) [Strategic Planning]( strategic planning) [Foreign Relations]( foreign relations) [Emergency Management]( emergency management) [National Security]( national security) [Current Leadership]( current leadership) [Supreme President Leo Duprey]( supreme president leo duprey) [Hélène Marchand]( h l ne marchand) [Alain Mercier]( alain mercier) [Security]( security) [Daily Life]( daily life) [Cultural Significance]( cultural significance) [Common Sayings]( common sayings) ["All roads lead to Continuity."]( all roads lead to continuity) ["The Palace remembers."]( the palace remembers) ["Ask the Tower."]( ask the tower) [Rumors and Secrets]( rumors and secrets) [Traveller Information]( traveller information) [Adventure Hooks]( adventure hooks) Overview The Palais de Continuité (Palace of Continuity) serves as both the administrative heart of Jardin and the symbolic embodiment of the world's political philosophy. Standing atop the heights overlooking central Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne, the palace dominates the skyline and serves as the seat of the Supreme Presidency, the Supreme Directorate, and many of Jardin's most influential ministries. To the citizens of Jardin, the palace represents stability, order, and the promise that each generation will improve upon the achievements of those that came before. Images of its distinctive towers appear on government broadcasts, educational materials, currency, and public monuments throughout the world. Session 1 Note The transcript sometimes refers to the incident location as the Palace of Continuity, though the detailed scene takes place in the [[Hall des Futurs Choisis]] / Hall of Chosen Futures. Treat "Palace of Continuity" references in Session 1 as either broad government complex shorthand or transcript imprecision unless later clarified. To foreign observers, however, the palace often appears as something far more imposing the command center of one of the most organized and closely managed societies in the Solomani Confederation. History Colonial Administration (Years 0 120) The first government building on the site was little more than a fortified administrative center overlooking the original settlement of Sainte Jeanne. As the colony expanded, political authority became increasingly centralized. Successive governors added new offices, archives, and military command facilities. The Unification Crisis (Year 147) Political divisions nearly fractured the young colony during the Unification Crisis. Several competing political movements sought control of the growing world. The eventual victory of the Directorate resulted in the construction of a new governmental complex designed not merely to govern but to symbolize unity. Construction of the original Palace of Continuity began shortly thereafter. The Century of Planning (Years 280 450) As Jardin's population expanded into the billions, the palace became the center of increasingly sophisticated social planning efforts. Entire ministries devoted to population management, education, genetics, and economic coordination established permanent headquarters within the complex. Many of the structures visible today date from this period. Modern Era Under the leadership of Supreme President Leo Duprey, extensive renovations modernized the palace's infrastructure and security systems. Officially, these improvements were intended to improve administrative efficiency. Unofficially, many believe the renovations included extensive underground command facilities capable of directing military and civil operations during planetary emergencies. Architecture The palace complex occupies nearly six square kilometers of heavily developed government land. The architecture reflects traditional Solomani monumental design principles Massive scale Symmetry White stone facades Grand public spaces Elevated terraces Formal gardens Towering administrative spires The most recognizable feature is the Central Continuity Tower , which rises nearly four hundred meters above the surrounding city. At night, powerful illumination systems make the tower visible from nearly every district within Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne. Major Facilities Office of the Supreme Presidency The official office and residence of the Supreme President. Most executive decisions affecting Jardin ultimately pass through this office. The Presidential Wing contains private meeting rooms, secure communications facilities, emergency command centers, and ceremonial halls. Chamber of Continuity The most important political chamber on Jardin. This vast circular hall hosts Party Congress sessions National ceremonies State funerals Presidential inaugurations Major policy announcements The walls contain the names of every Supreme President in the history of the world. Hall of Founders A public museum dedicated to the early settlers of Jardin. Schoolchildren regularly visit as part of their civic education. The exhibits emphasize themes of sacrifice, scientific achievement, and collective responsibility. Directorate Wing The meeting place of the Supreme Directorate. This section contains offices for National Security Economics Social Development Education Colonial Affairs Genetics Foreign Relations Many of the most important decisions on Jardin are debated here before reaching the Presidency. Archives of Continuity One of the largest government archives in the Confederation. Contains Historical records Census data Administrative archives Colonial documents Legislative records Access is highly restricted. Several sections remain permanently classified. Government Functions The palace coordinates nearly every major function of planetary government. These include Executive Administration Direct oversight of government agencies and ministries. Strategic Planning Long term economic, demographic, and military planning. Foreign Relations Diplomatic coordination with neighboring systems and Confederation authorities. Emergency Management Planetary crisis response and disaster planning. National Security Coordination between military, intelligence, and internal security organizations. Current Leadership [[Leo Duprey|Supreme President Leo Duprey]] The current ruler of Jardin. A former Minister of Social Solidarity, Duprey rose through the Party apparatus over several decades. Supporters credit him with Economic expansion Political stability Increased military readiness Greater influence throughout the Pilgham region Critics claim he has centralized too much authority within the Presidency. Few make such criticisms publicly. [[Chief Helene Marchand|Hélène Marchand]] Chief of Staff Responsible for managing the Presidency's daily operations. Many observers believe she controls access to power more effectively than any cabinet minister. [[Alain Mercier]] Minister of Genetics One of the most influential figures in modern Jardin politics. His upcoming presentation at the next Party Congress has become the subject of widespread speculation throughout government and academic circles. Many believe he is positioning himself as a future successor to Duprey. Security Security at the Palace of Continuity is among the most extensive on the planet. Protective measures include Presidential Guard regiments Internal Security Directorate personnel Automated surveillance networks Biometric access controls Electronic counterintelligence systems Dedicated anti terror units Visitors should assume they are under continuous observation. Most are. Daily Life Despite its immense importance, much of the palace operates like a small city. Each day Tens of thousands of civil servants report for work. Diplomatic delegations arrive from across the Confederation. Government committees meet continuously. School tours move through public sections. Journalists attend official briefings. Security personnel conduct routine patrols. The majority of the palace is devoted to administration rather than politics. Cultural Significance Few structures carry greater symbolic importance on Jardin. Citizens commonly view the palace as proof that civilization can be directed through careful planning and competent governance. The palace appears regularly in Educational materials Recruitment campaigns Political broadcasts National celebrations Public art For many citizens, the palace represents the very idea of Jardin itself. Common Sayings "All roads lead to Continuity." Used when discussing problems that ultimately require government involvement. "The Palace remembers." A reference to the government's extensive archives and long institutional memory. "Ask the Tower." A sarcastic expression used when someone expects government intervention. Rumors and Secrets Common rumors include Secret genetic archives exist beneath the palace. A classified command bunker extends deep into the bedrock. Certain citizens have personal files far larger than normal. Succession planning for the Presidency has already begun. Hidden corridors connect the palace to military facilities elsewhere in the city. Whether any of these stories are true remains unclear. Traveller Information Visitors are generally permitted access to public portions of the complex. Restricted areas require Official sponsorship Government credentials Security clearance Foreign Travellers often encounter additional scrutiny. Imperial citizens in particular may find themselves subject to extensive questioning. Weapons are prohibited throughout most of the complex. Violations are dealt with swiftly. Adventure Hooks 1. A senior official disappears shortly before Party Congress. 2. Classified records vanish from the Archives of Continuity. 3. A foreign diplomat seeks discreet protection. 4. A whistleblower claims to possess evidence of a government conspiracy. 5. An assassination attempt threatens a major state ceremony. 6. A hidden chamber is uncovered during renovations. 7. Travellers are hired to recover stolen government data. 8. A presidential advisor secretly seeks passage off world. 9. An Internal Security investigation targets the wrong suspect. 10. Evidence suggests someone has been altering historical records for decades. gm Referee Notes The Palace of Continuity functions best as the political center of a campaign focused on intrigue, espionage, diplomacy, and conspiracy. Nearly every major organization on Jardin has representatives operating within the palace, making it an ideal location to introduce plots that affect the entire world. Many campaigns may begin here but discover that the true story extends far beyond its walls.

title: Leo Duprey
summary: Supreme President of Jardin at Le Palais de Continuité.
text: Leo Duprey Supreme President of Jardin Overview Leo Duprey is the Supreme President of Jardin and the current ruler of the world, governing from [[Le Palais de Continuité]]. A former Minister of Social Solidarity, he rose through the Party apparatus over several decades and is credited by supporters with economic expansion, political stability, and greater Confederation influence — while critics, few of whom speak publicly, say he has centralized too much authority in the Presidency. He dreams of extending Jardin's reach across the entire subsector, and Minister [[Alain Mercier]]'s planned revelation threatened the stable future that ambition rests on. Notable For Head of state and Party leader of Jardin. Rose through Social Solidarity to the Presidency. His subsector ambitions depend on the stability Mercier threatened. Ties [[Le Palais de Continuité]] [[Alain Mercier]] [[Social Solidarity]]

Xenobiology Problem]( the xenobiology problem) [Mercier's Secret]( mercier s secret) Overview The Jardins Fermés (Closed Gardens) are among the greatest scientific achievements of modern Jardin and one of the most recognizable landmarks on the planet. Stretching across nearly forty square kilometers beneath a network of massive environmental domes, the Gardens serve as the primary center for biological research, agricultural innovation, ecological engineering, and environmental sciences on Jardin. To the average citizen, the Gardens symbolize the practical benefits of scientific planning and long term investment. Generations of breakthroughs developed within the domes have transformed Jardin into one of the most productive and self sufficient worlds in the Solomani Confederation. To researchers, the Gardens are a place of discovery. To government planners, they are an investment in the future. To foreign intelligence services, they are among the most tempting targets in the sector. The Gardens' unofficial motto is widely known throughout Jardin "The Hall Plans the Future. The Gardens Build It." History The Agricultural Emergency The origins of the Gardens trace back nearly six centuries to a period known as the Agricultural Emergency . Rapid industrialization and population growth placed enormous pressure on planetary food production. Although outright famine never occurred, several years of declining yields convinced government officials that dependence upon natural agricultural systems represented a long term strategic vulnerability. The Ministry of Development proposed a bold solution. Rather than merely increasing farmland, Jardin would build controlled environments capable of producing food regardless of weather, disease, or environmental disruption. The first domes were constructed shortly thereafter. The Expansion Years Initial results exceeded expectations. Scientists quickly developed Disease resistant grain varieties High yield fruits Climate adapted vegetables Efficient hydroponic systems Artificial pollination methods Funding expanded dramatically. Each success generated political support for additional research. Within a century, the original agricultural station had grown into a vast scientific city. The Biological Revolution As genetic science advanced, the Gardens became the center of biological innovation on Jardin. Entire departments were created to study Plant genetics Ecological engineering Environmental simulation Medical botany Xenobiology Many of the technologies that define modern Jardin originated beneath the domes. The Modern Era Today the Gardens represent one of the largest integrated biological research facilities in the Confederation. Scientists from across Solomani space routinely seek positions within its laboratories. Many spend entire careers inside the complex. Architecture Unlike the monumental grandeur of the Palace of Continuity or the administrative efficiency of the Hall of Chosen Futures, the Gardens emphasize harmony between technology and nature. The facility consists of twelve primary domes connected by enclosed transit corridors. From orbit the complex resembles a chain of enormous crystalline bubbles stretching across the eastern edge of Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne. Visitors entering the Gardens encounter Vast indoor forests Artificial rivers Research habitats Botanical collections Climate controlled ecosystems Many first time visitors compare the experience to entering another world. Major Domes Dome One Conservatoire des Fondateurs Founders Conservatory The primary public section of the Gardens. Contains Historical exhibits Public gardens Educational displays Tourist facilities Nearly every schoolchild on Jardin visits at least once. Dome Two Terran Heritage Preserve Dedicated to preserving species and ecosystems originating on Terra. Features recreations of Temperate forests Grasslands Wetlands Mediterranean environments The preserve is both a research facility and a cultural monument. Dome Three Futures Agriculture Division Agricultural Futures Division The largest food production research center on Jardin. Researchers develop New crops Advanced hydroponics Vertical farming systems Soil enhancement technologies Many agricultural exports begin here. Dome Four Atmospheric Systems Laboratory Studies planetary climate systems. Research includes Weather control technologies Environmental stabilization Atmospheric processing Terraforming support methods Several projects support Confederation colony worlds. Dome Five Living Medicines Center One of the most valuable facilities on the planet. Specializes in Pharmaceutical plants Medical genetics Bioengineered treatments Regenerative medicine Numerous life extending therapies were developed here. Dome Six Aquatic Biosystems Facility Contains Freshwater ecosystems Marine habitats Fisheries research Water purification studies Several interior oceans and lakes occupy much of the dome's volume. Dome Seven Ecological Systems Laboratory Entire ecosystems are modeled within controlled environments. Researchers study Species interactions Population dynamics Environmental resilience Ecosystem collapse scenarios This dome functions as a living simulation laboratory. Dome Eight Advanced Genetic Research Division One of the most prestigious scientific facilities in Jardin. Research focuses on Population genetics Hereditary conditions Long term adaptation Genetic forecasting Many projects directly support the Hall of Chosen Futures. Dome Nine Xenobiological Annex Officially responsible for studying imported alien organisms. Access is heavily restricted. Most citizens know little about its operations. Many rumors originate here. Dome Ten Colonial Adaptation Center Develops biological solutions for harsh colony environments. Projects include Desert agriculture Arctic ecosystems High gravity adaptations Atmospheric tolerance research Dome Eleven Experimental Systems Division Supports unusual and high risk research. Most projects remain classified until completion. Dome Twelve Restricted Research Zone Official records describe the dome only as "Advanced Biological Studies." No public tours exist. No research summaries are released. No scientist discusses their work there. Daily Life The Gardens operate continuously. Thousands of personnel travel between domes every day. Common sights include Researchers carrying specimen cases Students attending lectures Maintenance crews tending ecosystems Autonomous service robots Scientific conferences Despite the scale of the facility, the atmosphere remains surprisingly relaxed. Many employees describe it as a university town hidden inside a research installation. Scientific Importance The Gardens have contributed to Increased agricultural production Extended life expectancy Reduced disease rates Environmental restoration projects Colonial development programs Many historians argue that no institution has contributed more directly to Jardin's prosperity. Public Perception The Gardens are one of the most trusted institutions on the planet. Citizens view them as evidence that science can improve everyday life. Public approval remains consistently high. A common saying states "If the Gardens cannot solve it, perhaps it cannot be solved." Notable Individuals [[Dr. Sophie Delacroix]] Director General of the Gardens Widely regarded as one of the leading scientific minds in the Confederation. Frequently consulted by both Supreme President Leo Duprey and Minister Alain Mercier. [[Professor Lucien Morel]] Chief Ecological Systems Analyst Known for developing several influential ecosystem modeling theories. Believes entire planetary biospheres can eventually be predicted mathematically. [[Dr. Isabelle Fournier]] Director of Medical Botany Responsible for multiple breakthrough therapies. A popular public figure due to her medical achievements. [[Dr. Gabriel Laurent]] Director of Xenobiology Rarely appears in public. His work within Dome Nine has generated considerable speculation. Security Most of the Gardens are open and welcoming. Some areas are not. Security is provided by Garden Security Directorate Ministry of Genetics Security Branch Internal Security Bureau Visitors quickly notice certain corridors and transit lines are inaccessible. Questions about these restrictions are politely ignored. Rumors The Silent Forest An ecosystem hidden within a restricted section of Dome Twelve. Researchers allegedly enter but rarely discuss what they observed. Mercier's Laboratory Many believe Alain Mercier maintains a private research facility somewhere beneath the Gardens. No evidence has ever surfaced. The Perfect Crop A genetically engineered plant capable of eliminating food shortages across hundreds of worlds. The government supposedly refuses to release it. Living Archive Some claim the Gardens preserve biological samples from every major family line on Jardin. Officials deny this. The Lost Species Several supposedly extinct Terran species are rumored to survive within hidden sections of the complex. gm Classified Information Project Verdant Horizon A highly classified initiative combining ecological forecasting with demographic modeling. Researchers attempt to predict how biological systems and human populations will evolve over centuries. Only a handful of senior officials possess access. Dome Twelve Contrary to public records, Dome Twelve is not a single facility. It contains an entire network of subterranean laboratories extending beneath the Gardens. Even many senior researchers are unaware of the complex's full extent. The Mercier Findings Several portions of Minister Alain Mercier's controversial upcoming Party Congress presentation originated from research conducted within the Gardens. What those findings reveal remains unknown. Session 2 Dome 2 Delivery During [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]], the party picked up a sealed crate from Dome 2 after pressing a one use communicator supplied by [[Lucin]]. A worker in blue overalls brought the crate out on a dolly and wished them good travels. The crate was delivered to [[Chief Helene Marchand]]'s secured residence and contained a corgi. The delivery may have been simple underworld favor trading, political contraband, or something connected to the Gardens' genetic work. Adventure Hooks The Escaped Specimen An experimental organism disappears from a secured laboratory. Officials want it recovered quietly. The Silent Dome An entire research team vanishes from Dome Twelve. Their final reports contain impossible data. Industrial Espionage A foreign corporation seeks assistance stealing agricultural research. The Lost Botanist A respected scientist disappears inside the ecological simulation domes. Security footage offers no explanation. The Impossible Plant A classified species begins appearing in public markets. No one knows how it escaped. The Hidden Tunnel Maintenance workers discover a forgotten section of the original Gardens buried beneath newer construction. The Xenobiology Problem Something inside Dome Nine may be far more intelligent than officials previously believed. Mercier's Secret The Travellers uncover evidence connecting the Gardens to the controversial findings scheduled for presentation at the next Party Congress. Several powerful factions suddenly become interested in their activities. gm Referee Notes The Gardens represent the optimistic face of Jardin. Unlike the Palace, which represents authority, or the Hall, which represents administration, the Gardens demonstrate tangible achievements. Visitors should leave impressed. The facility should feel inspiring rather than sinister. Only after spending time there should players begin to notice the locked doors, missing reports, classified projects, and unanswered questions hidden beneath the beauty of the domes. The greatest secrets on Jardin are not hidden in the Palace. They grow beneath glass.

title: Luc Girard
summary: Labor Coordinator at Transstar.
text: Luc Girard Labor Coordinator Overview Luc Girard is [[Transstar]]'s Labor Coordinator, assigning thousands of dockworkers and logistics personnel across the Rousseau industrial levels. Officially he manages staffing; unofficially he can make careers appear or disappear, and his influence among working class Party members is considerable. In a company town, the man who controls the shifts controls a great deal more than the schedule. Notable For Assigns thousands of dock and logistics workers. Can quietly make or break careers. Holds real sway among working class Party members. Ties [[Transstar]]

title: Lucien Roche
summary: Information Broker at Quartier Sainte-Liberté.
text: Lucien Roche Information Broker Overview Lucien Roche is an information broker in [[Quartier Sainte Liberté]] who can acquire almost anything — for the right price. In a district whose data markets trade secrets the way other places trade goods, Roche is one of the names that gets whispered when someone needs to know what the official record will not tell them. What he sells to the party across the table, he has likely already sold to two others. Notable For Deals in almost any information, for a price. A fixture of Sainte Liberté's data markets. Loyal to the transaction, not the client. Ties [[Quartier Sainte Liberté]]

title: Lucien Voss
summary: Senior Freight Broker at Transstar Sector Exchange.
text: Lucien Voss Senior Freight Broker Overview Lucien Voss is a senior freight broker and something of a legend along Broker's Row in the [[Transstar Sector Exchange]], capable of arranging transport to almost anywhere — for a price. For a party that needs to move cargo, people, or itself off Jardin without answering identity questions, a broker of Voss's reach is exactly the sort of contact worth cultivating. The price, of course, is never only money. Notable For Can arrange freight to nearly any destination. A legend of the Exchange's Broker's Row. A plausible route off world for those who can pay. Ties [[Transstar Sector Exchange]]

title: Lucin
summary: Armored Sainte-Liberte data broker who gave the group a trike in exchange for a daylight delivery.
text: Lucin Overview Lucin is an armored data broker encountered in [[Quartier Sainte Liberté]] during [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]]. He operated from a dark alley market where credits were exchanged for data chips. Lucin wore armor and had a cybernetic third arm emerging from his back. He was cautious at first, but Dan and the supply team opened a working relationship. Known Services Data brokerage. Possible transport contacts. Access to an ammunition broker in [[Transstar Sector Exchange]]. Underworld errands and trust building jobs. Session 2 Deal Lucin offered the group a trike if they picked up a 36 by 20 ish crate from Dome 2 of [[Les Jardins Fermés]] and delivered it during daylight to an address he provided. The group completed the errand and discovered the destination was the secured residence of [[Chief Helene Marchand]]. The crate contained a corgi. The trike is not immediately reported stolen; Lucin said the people who bought it will not realize one vehicle is missing from a larger lot for months or years. Open Questions Does Lucin work for [[Marcel Delphine]], the [[Jardin Syndicate]], or a separate underworld network? Why did Lucin need outsiders with disguised identities for the delivery? Can he safely arrange ammunition or other supplies through Transstar? What does he know about Chief Helene Marchand? gm GM Notes The party intentionally avoided dropping Marcel Delphine's name while speaking with Lucin.

title: Maëlle Fournier
summary: Engineer and damage-control specialist aboard the TSS Profondeur.
text: Maëlle Fournier ![Maëlle Fournier portrait](/wiki/media/Maelle Fournier.png) Engineer / Damage Control Overview Maëlle Fournier is the engineer and damage control specialist aboard the [[TSS Profondeur]]. She is former Jardin Navy, experienced with the vessel's pipes, repairs, sensors, and combat damage. She introduces herself carrying a sensor in one hand and a welding tool in the other, making clear that anyone aboard the Profondeur needs to be useful rather than merely taking up air. Session 4 Fournier helps orient the party toward shipboard repair expectations and the reality of undersea salvage work. Her role frames the technical side of the Hadal mission pressure, seals, welding, power, and keeping old systems alive long enough to survive.

title: Mara Kovalenko
summary: Director of Foreign Trade Relations at Transstar Sector Exchange.
text: Mara Kovalenko Director of Foreign Trade Relations Overview Mara Kovalenko directs Foreign Trade Relations at the [[Transstar Sector Exchange]], managing its dealings with Imperial and Hive commercial interests. She holds one of the largest diplomatic contact networks in the subsector, the kind of address book that makes a person useful to intelligence services whether or not she works for them. Through her, the Exchange speaks to powers the Confederation prefers to keep at arm's length. Notable For Manages Imperial and Hive commercial relations. Holds a vast subsector wide contact network. A natural conduit to — and target of — foreign interests. Ties [[Transstar Sector Exchange]]

title: Marcel Delphine
text: Marcel Delphine The Shepherd of Lost Futures Designation Marcel Delphine | Type NPC | TL 14 | Status Active | Owner GM ![marcel delphine.jpg](/wiki/media/marcel delphine.jpg) | Field | Value | | | | | Designation | Marcel Delphine | | Nickname | The Shepherd | | Type | NPC | | Tech Level | 14 | | Brain Type | Organic (Uplifted Dolphin) | | Speed | Grav Frame 6m | | Hits | 24 | | Protection | 8 | | Cost | Not applicable | Overview Marcel Delphine is believed to be the leader of the Jardin Syndicate, one of the largest criminal organizations operating within the Jardin Subsector. To SolSec he is a trafficker, smuggler, forger, and criminal mastermind. To thousands of refugees, migrants, and political undesirables, he is a savior who provided opportunities that governments denied. Session 1 First Contact After the [[Mercier Assassination]], Marcel arranged for a driverless grav speeder to extract the group from the area around the [[Hall des Futurs Choisis]]. The vehicle carried them through waste disposal and service routes beneath [[Arcosphere Rousseau]] to a hidden, humid chamber behind a vault door. Marcel introduced himself as a member of the [[Jardin Syndicate]] and explained why the Syndicate wanted the group alive The Syndicate initially feared [[Alain Mercier]] had discovered their genetic code manipulation. They pulled back after learning Mercier's evidence pointed "from above, not below." Marcel believes the assassination and frame up may be used to blame the Syndicate anyway. Keeping the group alive may expose the people who silenced Mercier. Marcel gave the group [[Identity Veils]] and a one use communicator. He also claimed to possess unedited footage of the assassination and offered it in exchange for future cooperation. Claims Made The characters were selected because their military backgrounds and prior connections could be shaped into a believable assassin cell story. The public version of the assassination is edited or fabricated. The real guilty party is connected to the secret Mercier meant to reveal. If the group finds who silenced Mercier, they may also find evidence that clears their identities. An uplifted dolphin of advanced age, Delphine is rarely seen in public. When he does appear, he does so within a custom gravitic life support frame that resembles a floating throne draped in deep blue robes embroidered with ancient Terran symbols. Delphine presents himself not as a crime lord but as a social philosopher. He openly argues that governments have become obsessed with managing populations rather than helping individuals. His most famous saying is "A government plans futures. I help people choose them." No public evidence has ever connected him directly to criminal activities, yet nearly every intelligence agency in the sector believes he sits at the center of a vast network of smugglers, corrupt officials, transport companies, and identity brokers. Many believe he is the most dangerous man on Jardin. Many others believe he is the most compassionate. title: Mentor Jean Mercier
summary: Senior Creche Mentor at Crèche District 14.
text: Mentor Jean Mercier Senior Creche Mentor Overview Mentor Jean Mercier is one of the oldest serving mentors in [[Crèche District 14]]; three generations of graduates have passed through his Maison. He represents the institutional memory of Jardin's creche system, a living link between the children of today and the adults the system produced decades ago. Whether his surname connects him to the late minister is not established. Notable For Three generations of creche graduates raised in his Maison. Embodies the creche system's institutional memory. Surname link to Alain Mercier is unconfirmed. Ties [[Crèche District 14]]

title: Mercier Assassination
summary: Minister Alain Mercier was killed at the Hall des Futurs Choisis after announcing that he would reveal corruption in Jardin's genetic records.
text: Mercier Assassination Overview On 143 1105, Minister [[Alain Mercier]] was killed inside the [[Hall des Futurs Choisis]] shortly after the player characters were summoned there for official review. A news broadcast immediately beforehand reported that Mercier intended to reveal corruption in the genetic files at the coming Party Congress. The killing appeared designed to implicate the gathered characters. Several characters noticed their own weapons shift, fire, or show signs of having fired without normal handling. [[Ciernan Seanislav (Peter)]] found a round missing from his shotgun and the weapon hot. Mercier was struck by multiple shots and died despite immediate attempts to help him. Confirmed Facts Mercier had publicly announced that he had found corruption in the genetic affairs files. The characters were assembled in an unusually armed group at the Hall. Mercier passed through the office area with urgency before being shot. The shots were tied to or framed as coming from the characters' weapons. Mercier carried a locked tablet/pad and a phone. Mercier wore concealed armor, but the shots penetrated it. The public story was altered almost immediately into a terrorist narrative. Uncertain or Suspected The method used to manipulate or spoof the weapons is unknown. The identity of the person or group "above" Mercier is unknown. [[Marcel Delphine]] claims the [[Jardin Syndicate]] has unedited footage proving the characters did not shoot Mercier. Marcel claims Mercier's true discovery pointed upward within the system, not at Syndicate genetic fraud. Data recovered in [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]] suggests Mercier was killed for genetic marker research tied to extraordinary or psionic like effects. The same data may provide a possible avenue for understanding the impossible weapon or bullet behavior. title: Mercier Frame-Up
summary: The official story falsely blamed the Mercier assassination on the player characters and genetic outcasts.
text: Mercier Frame Up Overview After [[Alain Mercier]] was killed, the official narrative rapidly reframed the event as a terrorist action by genetic "half breeds" whose genetic identities were supposedly insecure. The news story included fabricated or edited footage, including a false image of [[Zoy (Damon)]] throwing a grenade at Mercier. The frame up also accused the group of killing Mercier's bodyguards. Some of that claim is misleading rather than wholly invented the group did kill Home Guard personnel during the escape, but after the situation had already turned violent and after Emma received a warning that the authorities intended to kill them. Why the Group Was Vulnerable The characters were gathered in one room despite several having prior military connections. They were allowed in armed because military veterans and retired service personnel may carry weapons with proper IDs. Several already knew one another, making it easy to portray them as an existing cell. Their mixed backgrounds, non human members, and criminal or intelligence ties made them easy propaganda targets. Evidence and Counter Evidence [[Marcel Delphine]] says the [[Jardin Syndicate]] has unedited footage. [[Emma Colbert (Laura)]] has a recording of the "kill them all" warning/order from her setup. Mercier's locked pad may contain relevant evidence. The public footage is known to include fake material. The [[Mobile Data Tube]] recovered in [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]] contains data suggesting Mercier was killed for the information he received. [[Inspector Marc Valois]] and SolSec are being denied access by Social Solidarity, creating a possible non planetary evidence channel. Open Questions Who built the false news package so quickly? Who ordered Social Solidarity or Home Guard to kill the witnesses? What will [[Elena Verona]] say as the surviving commissar? Will the Friday hearing reveal who benefits from the cover story? Can the recovered [[Mercier Genetic Findings]] be used without exposing the party to another trap?

title: Mercier Genetic Findings
summary: Recovered research data suggests decades of genetic-marker tests tied
text: Mercier Genetic Findings Overview The Mercier genetic findings are recovered research notes from the [[Mobile Data Tube]] intercepted in [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]]. The data appears to be part of what [[Alain Mercier]] planned to reveal before his assassination. The notes describe roughly fifty years of genetic tests and documentation. The file is corrupted near the end, so the final conclusion is missing. Extraordinary Effects The data correlates multiple genetic markers with unusual, possibly psionic or otherwise enhanced effects. Known examples from the file include Subject 18 predicted a random matter generator 214 consecutive times. Subject 21 consistently identified concealed playing cards. Other references imply remote perception, precognition, or similarly abnormal cognition, but the transcript does not preserve every detail. Marker Notes Laura's science review identified the following HX 14 Unequivocally alien genetic material; not uplifted Terran animal origin. SC 9 Solomani genetic code marker and a passable gene within Solomani genetic records. MY22 A duplicated genetic frailty or error, the sort of thing normally treated as a defect. PX 4 Non Solomani genetic material; possibly another human lineage rather than fully alien. Ciernan compared the notes to his own genetic papers. He does not have the identified markers. Why It Matters The data may explain why Mercier was killed. It may also give the party a possible explanation for the impossible behavior of the bullets during the assassination the conspiracy may involve psionic, genetic, or exotic biological technology rather than simple remote weapon control. Open Questions Do any of the player characters have these markers? Are the official genetic records trustworthy? Who ran the fifty year testing program? Were Mercier's findings hidden because they undermine Jardin's ideology, because they expose alien inheritance, or because they reveal useful abilities? Is the corrupted ending recoverable from another source? Did the weapon manipulation depend on these markers? Research Note 117A Research Note 117A Dr. Alain Mercier Longitudinal Population Cohort Analysis Over the last 43 years, twelve genetic markers have shown statistically impossible divergence from expected Solomani baseline. While individually insignificant, together they correlate strongly with unusual neurological development. The probability of this occurring naturally is less than 1 in 2.8 billion. Recommendation Expand cohort study. Correlation Table Marker Correlation HX 14 0.83 (Alien) SC 9 0.79 (Sol gene) MY 22 0.74 (Genetic Error on both sides) PX 4 0.69 (Non Human) Combined neurological variance 97.2% Research Notes Individuals carrying six or more identified markers demonstrate measurable increases in pattern recognition, intuitive reasoning, spatial cognition, and anticipatory decision making. Military simulations consistently place these individuals in the top 0.1% of all tactical performance. Then another document... Internal Memo Ministry of Genetics Subject Project HELIX Recent neurological studies continue to demonstrate measurable improvements in cognition among Cohort Sigma. While no evidence of psionic capability has been demonstrated, further investigation is recommended. Social Solidarity has requested expanded screening of all newborn citizens beginning next fiscal year. Mercier has written in red ink across the page "This statement is false." Then another file. Private Notebook We continue pretending this is about intelligence. It is not. The probability curves continue to climb. We have now documented twenty three individuals demonstrating events that cannot be explained by coincidence. Next page. Subject 18 predicted the random number generator 214 consecutive times. Next page. Subject 21 consistently identified concealed playing cards. Next page. Subject 09 accurately described a room on another floor. Next page. These are not isolated events. They are being ignored. Then... Email Draft (Never Sent) To Supreme Presidium Scientific Committee The current explanation of statistical error is no longer scientifically defensible. The data increasingly suggests the deliberate introduction of heritable neurological modifications into the population. I cannot yet determine whether this was intentional, accidental, or the result of an earlier classified program. If confirmed, this represents the largest unauthorized human genetics experiment in Confederation history. Finally, the thing that really gets their attention. Observation Log There is another possibility I have been unwilling to consider. The modifications are not producing EEFFCDSRdfsdrSDFE data corruption They have been doing it for years....

title: Mercier Lookalike Survivor
summary: Initial name for the Hadal survivor before he woke and identified himself as the restored Alain Mercier.
text: Mercier Lookalike Survivor This page records the party's initial identification of the Hadal survivor. As of [[Session 5 The Oduya]], he is known to be [[Alain Mercier]] restored through the [[Clone Rebirth Program]]. Overview The Mercier Lookalike Survivor is the only living person recovered from the sealed habitat at [[Hadal Research Site]]. He wears a Jardin Navy uniform and strongly resembles assassinated Genetics Minister [[Alain Mercier]]. Session 4 The party rescues four survivors from the sealed chamber, but three die after transfer. This survivor is stabilized at [[Undersea Base Elyon]] after emergency treatment with nanites. [[Varian Svazz (Allen)]] first notices the resemblance. Once the survivor is stabilized, the rest of the party also recognizes the connection. SolSec Interest Saichi observes a [[SolSec Operative at Elyon]] entering the survivor's room and taking scans. Emma recognizes the likely purpose SolSec can compare hand structure, fingerprints, bone growth patterns, and genetic identity to test whether a person is a duplicate, clone, altered body, or genuine relative. Session 5 Identification The survivor wakes when [[Victor Mendes (Steinbach)]] and [[Emma Colbert (Laura)]] enter his medical room. He first reacts with fear because he has seen the assassination footage and believes Victor was one of the people who killed him. He gives his name as [[Alain Mercier]] and explains that his body is a prepared clone awakened through engram transfer. His restored memory is roughly six weeks old, so he does not remember the final evidence his previous body announced before the assassination. Mercier cannot legally return to Jardin's surface after a public death. He offers the party access codes to his house and computer if they keep him safe until he can leave on a Navy ship or equivalent off world transfer. Open Questions What evidence is hidden at Mercier's house and computer? Who destroyed the clone bodies at Hadal, and which future target did that enable? Can the party move Mercier off world before SolSec, Jardin Navy, or the conspirators take control of him?

title: Mercier's Locked Pad
summary: Locked tablet recovered from Alain Mercier's body; one wrong attempt used, four before it wipes.
text: Mercier's Locked Pad The minister's last secret, one bad guess from ash Overview Mercier's locked pad was recovered from [[Alain Mercier]] after his assassination. It is roughly Kindle sized and password protected, and it is almost certainly the reason he was killed with it still on his body — the killers wanted him silenced, not searched. The Lock The pad is protected by a wipe on failure lock five wrong password attempts destroy the data permanently. One wrong attempt has already been spent, which leaves four tries before the contents are gone for good. There is no way to tell from the outside how close a guess is, and a failed brute force earlier confirmed the counter is real rather than a bluff. That single burned attempt makes the pad as dangerous as it is valuable. Whoever opens it has to be right, and being wrong is not a delay — it is the loss of the only physical evidence Mercier left behind. Known Facts The pad was on Mercier's body when he was killed. An early hack attempt failed and burned one of the five tries. Four attempts remain before the pad wipes itself. Its contents are unknown to the party. At the end of [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]], the group still intends to revisit the pad, but has not opened it. Importance The pad is widely assumed to hold the evidence Mercier meant to present at the [[Friday Party Congress Hearing]] — the genetic findings the official record has since worked so hard to corrupt and bury. What is actually on it goes further than anyone at the table yet knows. gm GM Truth — What the Pad Contains The pad is Mercier's private working file, kept off every official system precisely because of what it proves. Cracking it reveals, in roughly this order There is a Psi group inside [[Social Solidarity]]. A hidden cadre operating behind the ministry's Office of Exceptional Citizens and Office of Social Forecasting — the same people who are supposed to manage extraordinary citizens are quietly composed of them. Mercier's notes state plainly that they are "not fully human" living carriers of the very markers (HX 14, SC 9, MY22, PX 4) his research tied to psionic like ability in the [[Mercier Genetic Findings]]. They took power by inverting the Perfection System. The Psi group has climbed by lying that high ranking officials carry bad genetics — fabricating "defect" records for rivals and then presenting themselves as the discreet fixers who will keep the shameful results quiet. The threat of a manufactured genetic scandal, and the "favor" of covering it up, is the leverage that has put their people into position across the government. They have been hoarding the markers they call defects. The same HX /SC /MY /PX markers the group brands as flaws in their enemies, they have been quietly concentrating in their own bloodlines for two generations. The Perfection System's stated goal and the Psi group's actual breeding program are opposites wearing the same uniform. The assassination was a demonstration, not just a silencing. The "impossible" behavior of the weapons at the [[Mercier Assassination]] — rounds that curved, guns that spoofed — was the Psi group showing what it can do, then pinning it on the party through the [[Mercier Frame Up]]. Mercier suspected this before he died and says so. A short list of the ruined. The pad names several officials the group has already broken or is actively blackmailing with false genetic records, including at least one figure close to the Supreme Presidency. It does not confirm whether [[Leo Duprey]] is a protector of the group, a target of it, or unaware — Mercier ran out of time. It is partly a message. The final entries are addressed to whoever opens the pad. Mercier expected to be killed and left instructions trust the markers, not the ministry; and assume that the act of cracking the pad may itself trip a flag the Psi group is watching for. Running it the five strike wipe is the whole tension — the players will want to bring the pad to someone who can crack it ([[Lucin]], a Syndicate specialist, [[Inspector Marc Valois]]'s people) and every such contact is a chance for the Psi group to hear about it. A wrong guess doesn't just fail; it destroys the campaign's cleanest proof and hands the group's future entirely to unreliable testimony. title: Miasma
summary: A low-key destination one jump from Jardin, considered as a possible escape target.
text: Miasma Contents [Overview]( overview) [Session 1 Notes]( session 1 notes) Overview Miasma is described in the transcript as a relatively low key jump destination one jump from [[Jardin]]. [[Judith Dumont (Carla)]] considered it as a possible escape destination and hoped [[Keith Morris]] could help with plans to get there. Session 1 Notes Directly jumping from Jardin is difficult because of passport and identity controls. Keith Morris advised that moving to another planet within the Jardin system first may be easier than leaving directly from Jardin. Miasma remains a possible later destination once identity or transit problems are solved.

title: Mobile Data Tube
summary: Self-moving pipe courier recovered from the Hall; it carried a data chip tied to Mercier's genetic findings.
text: Mobile Data Tube Contents [Overview]( overview) [Payload]( payload) [Capabilities]( capabilities) [Party Handling]( party handling) [Open Questions]( open questions) Overview The mobile data tube is a cigar sized metal cylinder recovered from a bathroom drain inside the [[Hall des Futurs Choisis]] during [[Session 2 Masks and Markers]]. [[Dr. Luc Moreau]] placed a data stick into the tube, typed a warning message on an arm computer, put the tube in the toilet, and flushed it. The tube then extended small legs and tried to travel through the pipes to a recovery point. Payload The tube carried a data chip connected to [[Mercier Genetic Findings]]. The intercepted message said this was the last time the sender would pass information and that Mercier had obviously been killed for the data he received. Capabilities Navigates plumbing or pipes to a recovery point. Carries a data chip or data stick. Has leg like appendages for movement. Includes a destructive charge sufficient to destroy its contents if needed. Party Handling Zoy and Cass recovered the tube before it escaped. Emma disarmed its destructive charge, stopped the moving legs, and preserved the data chip. Open Questions Who was meant to receive Moreau's tube? Who was meant to recover it? Was Moreau part of Mercier's source network? Can the tube's routing or hardware identify other conspirators?

title: Nadia Giroux
summary: Investigative Journalist at Arcosphere Rousseau.
text: Nadia Giroux Investigative Journalist Overview Nadia Giroux is an investigative journalist working out of the Rousseau Arcology, known for exposing corruption and embarrassing powerful people who assumed their arrangements were private. She receives anonymous threats frequently and ignores them just as frequently. On a world where [[Social Solidarity]] curates the official narrative, a reporter who publishes uncomfortable truths is both a rare asset and a standing liability, and her continued freedom to work says as much about who protects her as about her nerve. Notable For Exposes corruption among Rousseau's powerful. Receives — and ignores — regular anonymous threats. A potential source or ally for anyone investigating official cover ups. Ties [[Arcosphere Rousseau]]

title: Nadine Pelletier
summary: Passenger Services Director at Transstar.
text: Nadine Pelletier Passenger Services Director Overview Nadine Pelletier is [[Transstar]]'s Passenger Services Director and the public face of the line's luxury travel, overseeing the arrival of VIPs, Party officials, and wealthy travelers at the Jardin Orbital Terminal. Charismatic and media savvy, she manages the experience of the powerful as they move through Jardin. Rumor holds that she knows every secret carried by every important passenger — a currency worth more than any fare. (No relation to Governor Adrien Pelletier of Rousseau.) Notable For Oversees VIP and Party official travel. Charismatic, media trained public face of Transstar luxury. Said to know every important passenger's secrets. Ties [[Transstar]]

title: Nico Gay
summary: Emma Colbert's smuggler contact; a mid-tier smuggler loyal to Emma within limits.
text: Nico Gay Overview Nico Gay is the son of Sarah Gay and a mid tier smuggler contact of [[Emma Colbert (Laura)]]. The transcript describes him as oddly loyal to Emma, provided she does not ask him to betray family or front crew. He gave Emma background on [[Marcel Delphine]] and the [[Jardin Syndicate]], saying the Syndicate is unlikely to betray the group as long as they deal honestly while down and out. Appears In [[Session 1 Official Business]] Information Provided The Jardin Syndicate often helps people who are less genetically pure by creating or altering genetic identities. The Syndicate is generally useful to the desperate or excluded. The [[Transstar Sector Exchange]] is an independent legal entity and potential refuge if the group's identity veils begin to fail. Name Note The transcript identified him by family connection rather than personal name; Nico Gay is an assigned campaign name.

title: Oduya
summary: Forty-year-old smuggling ship-boat raised by the party after the Hadal rescue.
text: Oduya Overview Oduya is the true name of the [[Sunken Ship Boat]] raised by the party during [[Session 5 The Oduya]]. It is a small craft capable of reaching orbit and other planets in the system, but it has no jump drive. The name means "openness." The craft had spent roughly forty years underwater before the party found it. Condition Found The hull was pressure damaged and partly buried in silt and sea growth. Four crew were dead aboard, including a captain found in a locker. One crew member was an uplifted gorilla. The bridge or pilot compartment suffered a pressure blowout. Reactor leakage once made the wreck dangerous enough that official investigators avoided full recovery. The craft carried removable false markings rather than painted permanent Navy identification. Recovery [[0 31 Saichi Maru (Annette)]] reached the wreck first, documented the exterior, recorded the dead crew, and spotted the removable markings. The rest of the party arrived with the [[TSS Profondeur]], patched the hull, restored partial power, drained water, booted the computer, and got the craft moving. The Profondeur briefly acted as a decoy when a small unresponsive craft approached the salvage site. Logs Oduya was a smuggling craft doing business with the [[Jardin Syndicate]] and dolphin contacts. It carried goods for underwater pickup and changed its apparent identity through removable transponders and exterior wraps. The ship was lost after a Navy patrol caught it during a drop. Oduya dove to escape the surface craft, but the patrol used depth charges. The pressure shock injured or killed the crew before they could recover. Cargo Recovered Common raw materials, mostly corroded or low value. Autorifles destroyed by water exposure. Illegal cybernetic weapons and implants. A valuable living tree in a coded hibernation chamber. The [[Transponder Swap Box]] held by the dead captain. Use to the Party Once repaired, Oduya can move [[Alain Mercier]] off world or into orbit without returning him to the surface. It also gives the party a system scale craft with changeable identities, useful for reaching other planets before they acquire a jump capable ship.

title: Philippe Laurent
summary: Fleet Maintenance Director at Transstar.
text: Philippe Laurent Fleet Maintenance Director Overview Philippe Laurent is [[Transstar]]'s Fleet Maintenance Director, responsible for keeping over four hundred vessels running across the region. Famous for his obsession with preventative maintenance — "Ships don't fail. Managers fail." — he holds his engineers to a standard that terrifies them and keeps Transstar's hulls in the sky. When a Transstar ship is sound, it is because Laurent refused to let it be otherwise. Notable For Maintains a regional fleet of 400 plus vessels. Fanatical about preventative maintenance. His engineers fear disappointing him more than any inspector. Ties [[Transstar]]

title: Pierre Gauthier
summary: Student Activist at Quartier Danton.
text: Pierre Gauthier Student Activist Overview Pierre Gauthier is a student activist and rising political figure in [[Quartier Danton]], closely watched by [[Social Solidarity]]. In a district built around the University of Jardin and the Party academies, a charismatic organizer who draws crowds is precisely the kind of person the state monitors before he becomes a movement. His trajectory could make him an ally, a martyr, or a recruit, depending on who reaches him first. Notable For A rising figure in Danton's student movement. Under active Social Solidarity surveillance. Could become an ally, an asset, or a cautionary tale. Ties [[Quartier Danton]] [[Social Solidarity]]

[Naval Investigation]( naval investigation) [The Ghost Ship]( the ghost ship) [The Shepherd's Invitation]( the shepherd s invitation) Overview The Port Sainte Jeanne Downport is the primary surface gateway to Jardin and one of the busiest starports in the Solomani Front. Every day thousands of passengers and millions of tons of cargo pass through its terminals. The Port serves as the physical connection between Jardin The Solomani Confederation The Imperial Border The Hive Federation The Frontier Worlds Most visitors see the Palace of Continuity as the symbol of Jardin. Most residents know the truth. The Port keeps the world alive. First Impressions The first thing visitors notice is the scale. The second is the noise. The third is the smell. Fuel. Industrial lubricants. Imported foods. Ocean air. Humanity. The Port never truly sleeps. Ships arrive at all hours. Cargo moves continuously. Announcements echo from towering terminals. Some visitors love it immediately. Others never feel comfortable here. History The Original Landing Field The first colonial settlement on Jardin was established near the present day Port. Its founders were Entrepreneurs Soldiers Adventurers Political dissidents Many arrived specifically to escape Imperial authority. Their descendants still celebrate this history. The Expansion Era As Jardin built its early empire, the Port expanded dramatically. Military shipyards. Colonial fleets. Trade convoys. Occupation forces. All departed from Port Sainte Jeanne. Some historians argue the Port was the true heart of the old Jardinese Empire. Modern Era Today the Port remains one of the largest transportation hubs in the subsector. Its facilities support Commercial traffic Naval logistics Colonial development Diplomatic missions Frontier exploration Layout The Port covers hundreds of square kilometers. Major sections include Arrival Terminal Complex Passenger processing center. Most visitors begin their journey here. Contains Customs Immigration Transportation links Hotels Currency exchanges The terminal handles millions of travelers every month. Cargo Basin Alpha The largest freight handling district. Dominated by Warehouses Cargo cranes Freight towers Container yards Thousands of workers operate here around the clock. Colonial Transit Zone Specialized facilities serving Frontier Colonies Development Projects Settlement Programs Many citizens beginning new lives pass through this district. It has become known as The District of Second Chances Orbital Elevator Complex A massive transportation system linking the downport to Port Sainte Jeanne Highport. The elevators operate continuously. Most cargo reaching orbit passes through these towers. Naval Interface Sector Joint facilities supporting Confederation Navy Home Forces Military Logistics Public access is heavily restricted. The Port Authority The Port is administered by the Port Authority of Jardin . Responsibilities include Traffic Control Safety Enforcement Infrastructure Management Customs Coordination The Authority works closely with Transstar Social Solidarity SolSec Confederation Navy Security The Port contains more law enforcement personnel than any other location on Jardin. Security organizations include Port Security Directorate Primary law enforcement agency. Handles Smuggling Violent crime Port security Cargo theft Customs Bureau Responsible for Import controls Export inspections Contraband interdiction Many traders fear Customs more than Port Security. Social Solidarity Monitors Returning citizens Immigration concerns Ideological risks Visitors often encounter them without realizing it. SolSec Liaison Office Handles Foreign intelligence threats Espionage Counter terrorism Officially a small office. Nobody believes this. Culture The Port is one of the least typical places on Jardin. People from across Charted Space pass through daily. Visitors include Merchants Colonists Diplomats Mercenaries Explorers Refugees As a result the Port possesses a reputation for being unusually open minded. At least by Jardinese standards. Neighborhoods The Sailor's Quarter The oldest district in the Port. Filled with Taverns Boarding Houses Restaurants Entertainment Venues A favorite destination for ship crews. Republic Market A sprawling commercial bazaar. Goods from hundreds of worlds can be found here. Many items are legal. Most are. Founder's Row Historic district preserving buildings from the original colony. Popular with tourists. The Freightlands Industrial district serving cargo workers. A rough area after dark. Organized Crime The Port has always attracted criminal organizations. Common activities include Smuggling Cargo theft Identity fraud Illegal migration Contraband trafficking The Jardin Syndicate maintains significant influence throughout the Port. The Syndicate Presence The Port serves as one of the Syndicate's most important operational zones. Common activities include Forged travel documents Unofficial shipping services Labor rackets Black market logistics Port Security fights a constant battle against them. Neither side expects victory. Notable Individuals [[Director Luc Beaumont]] Port Authority Director Responsible for overseeing the largest transportation facility on Jardin. Pragmatic and politically skilled. [[Commander Sophie Durand]] Port Security Directorate Veteran investigator known for her relentless pursuit of organized crime. [[Étienne Marchand]] Customs Commissioner A nightmare for smugglers. A hero to accountants. [[Captain Victor Mendes]] Transstar Freight Captain A respected merchant captain known throughout the Port community. Public Reputation Citizens often describe the Port as The Real Jardin Unlike the carefully managed government districts, the Port feels alive. Messy. Loud. Unpredictable. Successful. Rumors The Hidden Berth An unregistered landing field allegedly exists beneath the Port. The Ghost Manifest A cargo record from the Solomani Rim War appears in the system every year despite the ship having been destroyed centuries ago. The Shepherd's Dock A private landing zone supposedly controlled by Marcel Delphine. No one can prove it exists. The Missing Containers Entire cargo shipments occasionally vanish without explanation. Port officials deny this happens. Nobody believes them. Adventure Hooks Missing Passenger A prominent scientist disappears after arriving at the terminal. Customs Seizure A cargo container contains something far more dangerous than declared. Syndicate Courier The Travellers are mistaken for criminal couriers. Naval Investigation Military cargo disappears from the Naval Interface Sector. The Ghost Ship A vessel presumed lost decades ago suddenly requests docking clearance. The Shepherd's Invitation A message directs the Travellers to an unmarked warehouse in the Freightlands. Someone is waiting. gm Referee Notes Port Sainte Jeanne should feel very different from the rest of Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne. The Palace is power. The Hall is bureaucracy. The Gardens are science. Rousseau is society. The Exchange is money. The Port is movement. Everything arrives here. Everything leaves here. Ideas. Goods. People. Dreams. Criminals. Refugees. Spies. For many visitors, Port Sainte Jeanne is their first experience of Jardin. For many citizens, it is their last view of home. The Port is where the world meets the stars.

Most residents know the truth. The Port keeps the world alive. First Impressions The first thing visitors notice is the scale. The second is the noise. The third is the smell. Fuel. Industrial lubricants. Imported foods. Ocean air. Humanity. The Port never truly sleeps. Ships arrive at all hours. Cargo moves continuously. Announcements echo from towering terminals. Some visitors love it immediately. Others never feel comfortable here. History The Original Landing Field The first colonial settlement on Jardin was established near the present day Port. Its founders were Entrepreneurs Soldiers Adventurers Political dissidents Many arrived specifically to escape Imperial authority. Their descendants still celebrate this history. The Expansion Era As Jardin built its early empire, the Port expanded dramatically. Military shipyards. Colonial fleets. Trade convoys. Occupation forces. All departed from Port Sainte Jeanne. Some historians argue the Port was the true heart of the old Jardinese Empire. Modern Era Today the Port remains one of the largest transportation hubs in the subsector. Its facilities support Commercial traffic Naval logistics Colonial development Diplomatic missions Frontier exploration Layout The Port covers hundreds of square kilometers. Major sections include Arrival Terminal Complex Passenger processing center. Most visitors begin their journey here. Contains Customs Immigration Transportation links Hotels Currency exchanges The terminal handles millions of travelers every month. Cargo Basin Alpha The largest freight handling district. Dominated by Warehouses Cargo cranes Freight towers Container yards Thousands of workers operate here around the clock. Colonial Transit Zone Specialized facilities serving Frontier Colonies Development Projects Settlement Programs Many citizens beginning new lives pass through this district. It has become known as The District of Second Chances Orbital Elevator Complex A massive transportation system linking the downport to Port Sainte Jeanne Highport. The elevators operate continuously. Most cargo reaching orbit passes through these towers. Naval Interface Sector Joint facilities supporting Confederation Navy Home Forces Military Logistics Public access is heavily restricted. The Port Authority The Port is administered by the Port Authority of Jardin . Responsibilities include Traffic Control Safety Enforcement Infrastructure Management Customs Coordination The Authority works closely with Transstar Social Solidarity SolSec Confederation Navy Security The Port contains more law enforcement personnel than any other location on Jardin. Security organizations include Port Security Directorate Primary law enforcement agency. Handles Smuggling Violent crime Port security Cargo theft Customs Bureau Responsible for Import controls Export inspections Contraband interdiction Many traders fear Customs more than Port Security. Social Solidarity Monitors Returning citizens Immigration concerns Ideological risks Visitors often encounter them without realizing it. SolSec Liaison Office Handles Foreign intelligence threats Espionage Counter terrorism Officially a small office. Nobody believes this. Culture The Port is one of the least typical places on Jardin. People from across Charted Space pass through daily. Visitors include Merchants Colonists Diplomats Mercenaries Explorers Refugees As a result the Port possesses a reputation for being unusually open minded. At least by Jardinese standards. Neighborhoods The Sailor's Quarter The oldest district in the Port. Filled with Taverns Boarding Houses Restaurants Entertainment Venues A favorite destination for ship crews. Republic Market A sprawling commercial bazaar. Goods from hundreds of worlds can be found here. Many items are legal. Most are. Founder's Row Historic district preserving buildings from the original colony. Popular with tourists. The Freightlands Industrial district serving cargo workers. A rough area after dark. Organized Crime The Port has always attracted criminal organizations. Common activities include Smuggling Cargo theft Identity fraud Illegal migration Contraband trafficking The Jardin Syndicate maintains significant influence throughout the Port. The Syndicate Presence The Port serves as one of the Syndicate's most important operational zones. Common activities include Forged travel documents Unofficial shipping services Labor rackets Black market logistics Port Security fights a constant battle against them. Neither side expects victory. Notable Individuals [[Director Luc Beaumont]] Port Authority Director Responsible for overseeing the largest transportation facility on Jardin. Pragmatic and politically skilled. [[Commander Sophie Durand]] Port Security Directorate Veteran investigator known for her relentless pursuit of organized crime. [[Étienne Marchand]] Customs Commissioner A nightmare for smugglers. A hero to accountants. [[Captain Victor Mendes]] Transstar Freight Captain A respected merchant captain known throughout the Port community. Public Reputation Citizens often describe the Port as The Real Jardin Unlike the carefully managed government districts, the Port feels alive. Messy. Loud. Unpredictable. Successful. Rumors The Hidden Berth An unregistered landing field allegedly exists beneath the Port. The Ghost Manifest A cargo record from the Solomani Rim War appears in the system every year despite the ship having been destroyed centuries ago. The Shepherd's Dock A private landing zone supposedly controlled by Marcel Delphine. No one can prove it exists. The Missing Containers Entire cargo shipments occasionally vanish without explanation. Port officials deny this happens. Nobody believes them. Adventure Hooks Missing Passenger A prominent scientist disappears after arriving at the terminal. Customs Seizure A cargo container contains something far more dangerous than declared. Syndicate Courier The Travellers are mistaken for criminal couriers. Naval Investigation Military cargo disappears from the Naval Interface Sector. The Ghost Ship A vessel presumed lost decades ago suddenly requests docking clearance. The Shepherd's Invitation A message directs the Travellers to an unmarked warehouse in the Freightlands. Someone is waiting. gm Referee Notes Port Sainte Jeanne should feel very different from the rest of Nouvelle Sainte Jeanne. The Palace is power. The Hall is bureaucracy. The Gardens are science. Rousseau is society. The Exchange is money. The Port is movement. Everything arrives here. Everything leaves here. Ideas. Goods. People. Dreams. Criminals. Refugees. Spies. For many visitors, Port Sainte Jeanne is their first experience of Jardin. For many citizens, it is their last view of home. The Port is where the world meets the stars.

title: Prime Minister Bombing
summary: Reported terrorist bombing of the Prime Minister's home on the same day Mercier explains the clone backup threat.
text: Prime Minister Bombing Overview During [[Session 5 The Oduya]], news reports that the Prime Minister's home was bombed that morning. The broadcast describes the attack as suspected separatist terrorism and presumes the Prime Minister dead. The party recognizes the residence as the same place where the group previously delivered Lucin's sealed crate to [[Chief Helene Marchand]]. Why It Matters The bombing occurs shortly after [[Alain Mercier]] explains that the destruction of [[Hadal Research Site]] may have been a preparatory strike against clone backups. If a high ranking political figure had a prepared clone body at Hadal, destroying that backup first would make a later assassination permanent. Open Questions Was the Prime Minister actually killed? Did the Prime Minister have a clone backup at Hadal? Are suspected separatists responsible, or are they another cover story like the [[Mercier Frame Up]]? Did the bombing target the person, the residence, the staff, or records inside?

title: Professor Émile Laurent
summary: Political Theorist at Quartier Danton.
text: Professor Émile Laurent Political Theorist Overview Professor Émile Laurent is a political theorist and public intellectual based in [[Quartier Danton]], the capital's academic and congressional quarter. He appears frequently on state broadcasts, where his commentary lends scholarly weight to the Party's line. Whether he shapes official thinking or merely dresses it is a question his students debate more freely than he does. Notable For Prominent public intellectual and state broadcast regular. Lends academic authority to Party positions. Influential in Danton's university circles. Ties [[Quartier Danton]]

title: Professor Lucien Morel
summary: Chief Ecological Systems Analyst at Les Jardins Fermés.
text: Professor Lucien Morel Chief Ecological Systems Analyst Overview Professor Lucien Morel is Chief Ecological Systems Analyst at [[Les Jardins Fermés]], where he developed several of the ecosystem modeling theories the Gardens rely on. He believes that entire planetary biospheres can eventually be predicted mathematically, a conviction that fits neatly into a world convinced it can plan its own future. His models shape which experiments the domes pursue and which they quietly abandon. Notable For Author of influential ecosystem modeling theories. Believes planetary biospheres are ultimately predictable by math. His models steer research priorities across the domes. Ties [[Les Jardins Fermés]]
